chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: Backing Cab Calloway: Minnie the Moocher and conducting by ear
summary: Horace only backed Calloway when he played where Horace was house band. Cab was no musician but caught arrangements after a couple of rehearsals with help from pianist Benny Payne.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Yeah, you bet. Somewhere I was

reading that -- maybe it was one of the theater dates you did in New York with -- did you back Cab Calloway or you had some -- there was something I discovered, maybe on some recording date or something. Do you recall anything with Cab Calloway?
No, the only time I backed Cab was when he was booked into a club where I was the house band. And --
Huh. Maybe that's it. He was on the bill.

Yes, he was on the bill. This is when he did It Ain't Necessarily So and, of course, Minnie the Moocher, that was the theme song of his big band in those days. And I think how that came about, you know, he traveled -- the past few years he's been traveling with the Globetrotters, the famous basketball team, and during the intermissions, he's been doing the talking and the singing and whatnot. Well, here a few years (inaudible) back -- I had the pleasure of doing this on -- I think I was in Minneapolis. And he was booked into one of the clubs, and he had his music first -- and he knew exactly what he wanted, you know, naturally actually, because he was another guy like Lucky Millinder that would-- could conduct a band, you know, with the finesse, after he had heard the arrangement. He wasn't a musician. He didn't play anything.
But -- and Benny Payne, the great pianist, who is

now with the great Billy Daniels, was in Cab Calloway's band at that time, and was his pianist, you know. So Cab relied upon these guys in the -- he was the type of fellow that, if an arranger brought an arrangement in, he would let you rehearse the band, and he'd sit back, and you blew a couple of times go it over and he'd walk up to you and and Father Payne says, "I got it now."
